reasoning_traces.think:
The survey establishes that zero-shot video-LLMs fail in sports due to insufficient inductive bias, requiring domain adaptation. This failure mode is quantified by a 6% expert annotation bottleneck, which limits the applicability of general-purpose models. The dataset inventory reveals that while many datasets exist, they are unevenly distributed across sports and tasks. Soccer dominates with 74 datasets, whereas American football has minimal representation in NFL-specific contexts. The distribution of generative vs. discriminative paradigms (78.5% vs. 21.5%) suggests a preference for generative modeling in sports, though discriminative methods remain critical for action recognition. These findings imply that GSE must build upon fine-tuned models and curated datasets to achieve robust performance. The expert annotation bottleneck further necessitates Bayesian inference strategies to extract maximum signal from limited labeled data. The failure of zero-shot models highlights the need for structured, domain-specific training pipelines rather than relying on off-the-shelf architectures.
